In mysql dialect, it should be 
```sql
INSERT INTO t (col1,col2)  VALUES (%s, %s) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col2=coalesce(VALUES(col2), t.col2)
```

OK here is where that has to happen

```
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
index e0bf16793..167994121 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
@@ -1311,6 +1311,8 @@ class MySQLCompiler(compiler.SQLCompiler):
                 isinstance(val, elements.ColumnClause)
                 and val.table is on_duplicate.inserted_alias
             ):
+                # TODO: need to do a traversal here to find columns inside
+                # of functions / composed SQL
                 value_text = "VALUES(" + self.preparer.quote(column.name) + ")"
             else:
                 value_text = self.process(val.self_group(), use_schema=False)

```

here's a full POC, needs cleanup, correct  the imports, etc.

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
index e0bf16793..2fd33aa3f 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
@@ -1303,17 +1303,26 @@ class MySQLCompiler(compiler.SQLCompiler):
             if coercions._is_literal(val):
                 val = elements.BindParameter(None, val, type_=column.type)
                 value_text = self.process(val.self_group(), use_schema=False)
-            elif isinstance(val, elements.BindParameter) and val.type._isnull:
-                val = val._clone()
-                val.type = column.type
-                value_text = self.process(val.self_group(), use_schema=False)
-            elif (
-                isinstance(val, elements.ColumnClause)
-                and val.table is on_duplicate.inserted_alias
-            ):
-                value_text = "VALUES(" + self.preparer.quote(column.name) + ")"
             else:
+                def replace(obj):
+                    if isinstance(obj, elements.BindParameter) and obj.type._isnull:
+                        obj = obj._clone()
+                        obj.type = column.type
+                        return obj
+                    elif (
+                        isinstance(obj, elements.ColumnClause)
+                        and obj.table is on_duplicate.inserted_alias
+                    ):
+                        from sqlalchemy import literal_column
+                        obj = literal_column("VALUES(" + self.preparer.quote(column.name) + ")")
+                        return obj
+                    else:
+                        # element is not replaced
+                        return None
+                from sqlalchemy.sql import visitors
+                val = visitors.replacement_traverse(val, {}, replace)
                 value_text = self.process(val.self_group(), use_schema=False)
+
             name_text = self.preparer.quote(column.name)
             clauses.append("%s = %s" % (name_text, value_text))
 

```

Something to consider:

MySQL 5.7 reaches end of mainstream support (what Oracle calls "Premier Support") in October of this year (ref: [Oracle Lifetime Support Policy](http://www.oracle.com/us/support/library/lifetime-support-technology-069183.pdf), page 21).

The [MySQL documentation for INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/insert-on-duplicate.html) says

> The use of VALUES() to refer to the new row and columns is deprecated beginning with MySQL 8.0.20, and is subject to removal in a future version of MySQL. Instead, use row and column aliases, as described in the next few paragraphs of this section.

So within a few months the old VALUES() approach will be "fully" deprecated and the MySQL dialect should(?) start rendering statements like ...

```sql
INSERT INTO t (col1,col2) VALUES (%s, %s) AS inserted 
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col2=coalesce(inserted.col2, t.col2)
```

... which is very close to the "incorrect" way it is being rendered now.

Currently the dialect "fails" (to render the old-style SQL) without error. Rather than add a bunch of complexity to support the legacy approach, perhaps consider *detecting* the condition and then

- raise a `NotImplementedError` for MySQL versions < 8, and 
- render the new-style SQL for more up-to-date versions.

can't we still use VALUES like my patch does above for mysql < 8 ?  it seems like we should be using VALUES in most cases right now.  keep in mind MariaDB is here too.    whether to use VALUES or .inserted is just another MySQL /MariaDB version detection issue, we have plenty already.

> can't we still use VALUES like my patch does above for mysql < 8 ?

I'm sure we can, I was just suggesting an alternative that would avoid adding new code — code which would become obsolete relatively soon — to fix an issue that nobody has reported until now.

we are rendering VALUES right now and if im understanding correctly, it's going to break for newer MySQL versions at some point.  so we have to support both, because mysql 5.7 support is going to be for a long time as  well as mariadb support.
we need the above patch to go in at the very least in order to fix the immediate issue and it's fairly fundamental.   dealing with deprecated syntax for MySQL 8 can be separate.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Render VALUES within composed MySQL on duplicate key expressions** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/1767

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**Render VALUES within composed MySQL on duplicate key expressions** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/1768

issue.title: The on_duplicate_key_update method for MySQL renders with fixed columns names

labels.name: fairly easy
labels.description: maybe a little more involved than "easy' but still doable for motivated newcomers

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

When calling the `visit_on_duplicate_key_update` method, the compiled output will replace all the `insert_stmt.inserted` aliases to the one matching the `column.name`, even if the alias points to another object.
 
The issue could be considered a split-off from #5173, at https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/rel_1_3_24/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py#L1436, where it sets `"VALUES(" + self.preparer.quote(column.name) + ")"`.

I think the best way is to use `obj.name` instead of `column.name`.

Btw, the issue can be reproduced on both `1.3.24` and `1.4.26`.


### To Reproduce

```python
from datetime import datetime
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Boolean, DateTime, func
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base


Base = declarative_base()


class DebugTbl(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'debug_tbl'

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    enabled = Column(Boolean)
    updated = Column(DateTime)


entries = [
    {
        'name': 'first',
        'enabled': True,
        'updated': datetime.utcnow(),
    },
    {
        'name': 'second',
        'enabled': False,
        'updated': datetime.utcnow(),
    },
]

# check the insert/update against the `debug_tbl` table, with IF statement

insert_stmt = mysql.insert(DebugTbl).values(entries)
on_duplicate_key_stmt = insert_stmt.on_duplicate_key_update(
    name=func.IF(insert_stmt.inserted.updated > DebugTbl.updated,
                 insert_stmt.inserted.name,
                 DebugTbl.name),
    enabled=func.IF(insert_stmt.inserted.updated > DebugTbl.updated,
                    insert_stmt.inserted.enabled,
                    DebugTbl.enabled),
    updated=func.IF(insert_stmt.inserted.updated > DebugTbl.updated,
                    insert_stmt.inserted.updated,
                    DebugTbl.updated),
)
sql_statement = on_duplicate_key_stmt.compile(dialect=mysql.dialect())

assert sql_statement.string == (
    'INSERT INTO debug_tbl (name, enabled, updated) '
    'VALUES (%s, %s, %s), (%s, %s, %s) '
    'ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE '
    'name = IF(VALUES(updated) > debug_tbl.updated, VALUES(name), debug_tbl.name), '
    'enabled = IF(VALUES(updated) > debug_tbl.updated, VALUES(enabled), debug_tbl.enabled), '
    'updated = IF(VALUES(updated) > debug_tbl.updated, VALUES(updated), debug_tbl.updated)'
)
```


### Error

AssertionError

### Versions

- OS: Windows
- Python: 3.8.8
- SQLAlchemy: 1.3.24
- Database: MySQL 5.7.33
- DBAPI (eg: psycopg, cx_oracle, mysqlclient): pymysql 0.9.3


### Additional context

_No response_

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

Starting with mysql 8.0.20 we get a deprecated syntax warning from `on_duplicate_key_update`, and at some point this will break.

The cause and how to fix are explained in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/5173#issuecomment-593163758.  However I ran into this bug in the wild, and spent time tracking this down, so I'm putting it into the bug tracker with context for the next person who runs into this error.

Separate note.  I tried to do the `-Werror` flag and that somehow got in the way of connecting to MySQL.  That's not your bug, but is why I didn't give a stack backtrace as requested.

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy.dialect.mysql import insert 
from sqlalchemy import func
insert_stmt=insert(t).values(col1=1,col2=2)
upsert_stmt=insert_stmt.on_duplicate_key_update(col2=func.coalesce(insert_stmt.inserted.col2,t.c.col2))
```


### Error

```
/opt/homebrew/lib/python3.9/site-packages/aiomysql/cursors.py:239: Warning: 'VALUES function' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please use an alias (INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...) AS alias) and replace VALUES(col) in the ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE clause with alias.col instead
```
